pub struct Vec<T, A = Global> { /* private fields */ }

A contiguous growable array type, written as Vec<T>, short for 'vector'.

Vectors are a fundamental collection in Rust. They are stored on the heap and can grow or shrink at runtime. Indexing is O(1), pushing to the back is amortized O(1), and iteration is cache-friendly.

let mut v = Vec::new();
v.push(1);
v.push(2);
assert_eq!(v.len(), 2);
assert_eq!(v[0], 1);

Implementations

pub const fn new() -> Vec<T>

Constructs a new, empty Vec<T>. The vector will not allocate until elements are pushed onto it.

pub fn with_capacity(capacity: usize) -> Vec<T>

Constructs a new, empty Vec<T> with the specified capacity. The vector will be able to hold exactly capacity elements without reallocating.

pub fn push(&mut self, value: T)

Appends an element to the back of a collection. Panics if the new capacity exceeds isize::MAX bytes.

pub fn pop(&mut self) -> Option<T>

Removes the last element from a vector and returns it, or None if it is empty.

pub const fn len(&self) -> usize

Returns the number of elements in the vector, also referred to as its 'length'.

pub const fn is_empty(&self) -> bool

Returns true if the vector contains no elements.
